rationale: PINS protobuf's NAME RESOLUTION contract, which is the one rule in this analyzer that can silently point an edge at a type that exists in no file. The specification says a relative type name resolves from the INNERMOST enclosing scope outward, and that a leading dot makes the name ABSOLUTE. The file is built around a shape that is legal protobuf and that no other fixture in this lane has: a top-level `Inner` AND a nested `Outer.Inner`, so a resolver that starts its walk at the outermost scope, or that compares only the last dot segment, lands on a real-but-wrong symbol and passes every other row in the suite. Also pins the two fallback shapes, which are decided rather than guessed: an unqualified name not declared here resolves WITHIN the package by specification (`scope.v1.Imported`), while a dotted name not declared here falls back AS WRITTEN (`google.protobuf.Timestamp`) because protobuf writes multi-segment type names fully qualified in practice. Both fallbacks are the analyzer's declared boundary and are asserted here so a later change to them cannot pass unnoticed.

expectSymbols.name: Inner
expectSymbols.note: the TOP-LEVEL Inner. It exists so the nested one has something to be confused with.

expectSymbols.name: Inner
expectSymbols.note: the NESTED Inner: a distinct declaration from the top-level one, in the same file

expectSymbols.name: Inner
expectSymbols.note: qualifiedName carries the RESOLVED id, not the bare name, and it is carried on BOTH channels a consumer can reach. `s.qualifiedName` is the one the product reads: it survives pool-worker's symbol projection (metadata.id does not) and becomes brain_symbol.qualified_name, the column resolveRelationships strategy 1 matches a relationship's target against. `metadata.qualifiedName` is the one a fixture can assert, because run-fixtures.ts's CONSTRAINT_KEY_ALLOWLIST carries no `qualifiedName` key. Measured end to end through the real indexer and the real store over 40 reference .proto files (script/m14/tmp/protobuf/probe/store-binding.mts, two runs each): with qualified_name equal to the bare name, 0 of 3,075 analyzer edges were provably the declaration they named; with it equal to the id, 2,977 of 3,075 are (96.81%).

expectSymbols.name: Inner
expectSymbols.note: the SAME NAME, a second declaration, and the two qualifiedNames differ. This is the disambiguator a bare-name qualifiedName cannot carry, and it is what bb_impact needs: storeResults recovers a symbol's name by stripping the fileId prefix, so two same-named declarations in one file are separable only by their qualified spelling.

expectSymbols.name: top
expectSymbols.note: a FIELD, not only a type. A member is the endpoint of most `contains` edges, so a fix that published ids for types and left members bare would have moved nothing the graph actually walks.

expectSymbols.name: inner
expectSymbols.note: a field whose NAME equals the type it names (`scope.v1.Outer.Inner`). Both ids are published and both are distinct, which is what keeps the `uses` edge off the self-edge shape forbidRelationships asserts below.

expectSymbolCount.name: Inner
expectSymbolCount.note: exactly THREE declarations named Inner, and the third is the point of this file: the top-level TYPE (scope.v1.Inner), the NESTED type (scope.v1.Outer.Inner), and the shadowing FIELD (scope.v1.SelfNamed.Inner) whose name equals the type it names. A fourth would mean a type was published twice; two would mean the shadowing field was dropped, and the self-edge it used to produce would be back.

expectSymbolCount.name: Inner
expectSymbolCount.note: the shadowing field. Exactly one, published under the plain id — the type it names is a DIFFERENT declaration and must not be merged with it.

expectRelationships.note: THE scope-walk row. Written `Inner`, inside `Outer`, and `Outer` itself declares an `Inner`, so the innermost scope wins: scope.v1.Outer.Inner. Landing on the top-level scope.v1.Inner instead is the defect the scope chain exists to prevent, and a top-level `Inner` IS declared in this file so the wrong answer is a real symbol rather than a dangling name — which is what makes it hard to notice.
the same spelling one scope deeper, so a resolver that checked only the IMMEDIATE parent would miss it and fall through to the top level
fully qualified from the top level with NO leading dot, and still the global spelling. The package is scope.v1, so a prefixing resolver produces scope.v1.scope.v1.Outer.Inner.

the CONTROL for the two rows above: a bare `Inner` at file scope, where no enclosing scope declares one, so the top-level declaration is correct. Without this row an analyzer that always answered `Outer.Inner` would pass.

THE absolute row. `.other.v1.Thing` names the global type whatever the enclosing package is, so the target is other.v1.Thing and NOT scope.v1.other.v1.Thing. This is a different rule from the dotted-fallback row below and fails independently.
unqualified and not declared here: protobuf resolves such a name WITHIN the package by specification, so scope.v1.Imported is the correct target even though this file does not declare it

dotted and not declared here: falls back AS WRITTEN, because a multi-segment type name is written fully qualified in practice. Prefixing the package produces scope.v1.google.protobuf.Timestamp, a name in no file.

THE shadowing row, and a regression guard for a defect this lane measured and fixed. The field is NAMED `Inner` and its type is the top-level `Inner`, so the innermost scope candidate `scope.v1.SelfNamed.Inner` is the FIELD ITSELF — published moments before this edge is emitted. Resolving against every declaration answered the reference with the field and produced `scope.v1.SelfNamed.Inner -> scope.v1.SelfNamed.Inner`. The walk continues outward to the real type because only TYPES are in the resolution namespace. Measured before the fix: 9 such self-edges over 606 corpus files.

the CONTROL for the row above, with NO name collision: same resolver, same depth, nothing to shadow. A fix that simply stopped resolving relative names inside a message scope would pass the shadowing row and fail this one.

forbidRelationships.note: DELIBERATELY absent: the self-edge, and the exact shape of the 9 corpus defects. A field and a type colliding on one id is how a fabricated edge is born — bb_graph, bb_impact and bb_migrate would each read this as a field whose type is itself.

DELIBERATELY absent. The top-level `Inner` is a real declaration in this file, so this edge would resolve and read as plausible — which is exactly why it has to be forbidden explicitly. It is the wrong answer: the innermost enclosing scope that declares the name is `Outer`.
same wrong answer one scope deeper
the package-prefixed reading of a leading dot. The dot is what forbids it.
the package applied to an already-qualified name
the package applied to a dotted fallback
and the mirror image of the forbid above: a file-scope bare `Inner` must NOT reach into a nested scope. Pinning only the positive row would let an over-eager scope walk pass.
